title: States of Matter and Particle Models
purpose: Differentiate states of matter and phase transitions.
labDataRequirement: Particle model investigation of solids, liquids, gases, and phase transitions using diagrams or assigned virtual models.
safetyNotes: Use virtual/data-based models. No heating, boiling, freezing, glassware, or pressure containers without TOR-assigned controls.
simulationReview: Direct simulation/resource link is provided in P01.html and in directSimulationUrl.
assessmentStimulusNeeded: Use the Unit 1 matrix requirement for this lesson: embedded scenario, table, graph, model, diagram, or organizer as needed.
simulationVirtualLabReviewRequirement: Required for safety/procedure practice, measurement/data analysis, and particle models
simulationVirtualLabReviewFocus: Particle model investigation of solids, liquids, gases, and phase transitions
directSimulationStudentTask: After the simulation opens, use the screen that shows particles for solid, liquid, and gas behavior. Select or display one state of matter at a time: solid, liquid, then gas. Use the temperature or heating/cooling control only after recording the starting particle spacing and motion. Record a three-row table with state, particle spacing, particle motion, temperature or energy change, and the phase-change conclusion.
simulationReviewImplementation: Student-facing lesson includes one exact direct simulation/resource link plus adjacent step-by-step directions for what to open, click/use, observe, record, and connect to the lesson standard.
simulationSourceReference: PhET States of Matter; CK-12; OpenStax Chemistry 2e
